title: Two letters that ask you to stop and listen.
subtitle: Ha Mim opens the surah of the smoke
then: This surah came in Makkah, at a time when Quraysh were growing more hostile to the Prophet ﷺ. It opens with two letters, Ha and Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What they do for the listener is clear: they halt the ear before the message begins.
now: You open the app between two notifications. Your thumb is already looking for the next thing. Two letters you cannot explain sit at the top of the page. {idea}Let them slow you down for one breath.{/idea}
old: If I cannot explain a word, I can skip past it.
new: Some words are there to make me stop, not to be decoded.
try: Before you read today, put the phone face down for five seconds, then begin.

title: An oath by the Book that makes things clear.
subtitle: Why Allah swears by His own clear Book
then: The people of Makkah claimed the Quran was made up by the Prophet ﷺ. The surah answers by swearing by the Book itself. {idea}The Book that makes things clear is its own witness{/idea} to where it came from.
now: Someone in a group chat says it is just an old book, written by people. You have heard it and never really checked. {idea}The answer it gives is: read me and see how clear I am.{/idea}
old: I need outside proof before I take this Book seriously.
new: The Book asks to be weighed by its own clarity first.
try: Read one short passage slowly today and note one thing it made clear to you.

title: The Quran came down on a blessed night.
subtitle: Laylatul-Qadr, and why the warning is a gift
then: Ibn Kathir explains the blessed night as Laylatul-Qadr in Ramadan. Makkah treated the message as {trap}a disaster that had landed on them{/trap}. The verse says the hour it came was {reward}blessed{/reward}, and its warning tells people what is good for them and what harms them.
now: The doctor tells you your blood sugar is high. It ruins your afternoon. Years later you realise {reward}that appointment saved you{/reward}. A warning that arrives in time is a kindness, even when it stings.
old: A warning is bad news I would rather not hear.
new: A warning that comes in time is a mercy that came early.
try: Think of one warning you got this year and brushed off. Give it a second look.

title: On that night the year's matters are set out.
subtitle: Decrees that are wise and firm
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Umar, Mujahid and others that on this night {idea}the decrees of the coming year are passed to the angelic scribes{/idea}: life span, provision, and what will happen. The word hakim means decided and firm.
now: January. You buy a new planner and fill in goals, a budget, a holiday. You feel in charge. {idea}Plan anyway, but hold it lightly.{/idea} Your year is already known to the One who is wise.
old: My year will go the way I plan it.
new: I plan, and my year rests in a wise decree I can trust.
try: Look at one plan for this month and add a quiet in sha Allah to it.

title: Every matter comes as a command from Him.
subtitle: Nothing happens outside His leave and knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir says everything that happens and the revelation He sends down {idea}all comes by His command, by His leave and with His knowledge{/idea}. Sending messengers to people was an urgent need, and He met it.
now: The bus is late, the job offer comes, the test result is fine. You call it luck. {idea}The verse calls it a command that was sent.{/idea} That changes how you thank and how you wait.
old: Most of what happens to me is random.
new: What reaches me was sent, and guidance was sent too.
try: When something good happens today, say alhamdulillah instead of lucky.

title: The message is mercy from the One who hears.
subtitle: Revelation as care, not burden
then: Makkah was in the grip of a famine when this surah came, and its leaders wanted relief. The verse names the revelation itself as {reward}a mercy from your Lord{/reward}, sent by One who hears and knows.
now: You read a verse that asks something of you and feel the weight first. Picture a parent writing a note before a long trip: eat well, lock the door. {reward}That note is love written down.{/reward}
old: Religious guidance is mostly a list of demands.
new: The guidance is mercy from One who heard what I needed.
try: Pick one instruction you find heavy and ask: how could this be care for me?

title: Lord of everything, if you want certainty.
subtitle: The Sender of the Book owns the heavens and earth
then: Ibn Kathir says the One who sent the Quran is {idea}the Lord, Creator and Sovereign of the heavens and the earth{/idea} and all between them. The verse adds: if you have real certainty. The people of Makkah admitted Allah created all this, yet doubted His Book.
now: You believe Allah made the sky. You also check your horoscope app, just for fun. {trap}Certainty in one place, doubt in another.{/trap} The verse asks you to let the first certainty reach the second.
old: I believe in Allah, but I am not sure about the details.
new: If He owns everything, then His Book deserves the same certainty.
try: Go outside tonight, look up at the sky for a minute, and remember who sent the Book.

title: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.
subtitle: The One who gives life and takes it
then: Quraysh held on to idols because their ancestors did. The verse answers: {idea}He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers{/idea}. The ancestors were His creation too, and He gave them life and took it.
now: A family tradition you keep because "we always did it this way." Your grandmother's photo on the wall. {idea}The One who gave her life gave you yours.{/idea} Loyalty to her includes returning to Him.
old: Keeping family ways is how I honour those before me.
new: The truest link to my forefathers is the Lord we share.
try: Make a short dua for one grandparent or ancestor by name today.

title: They play around inside their doubt.
subtitle: Treating certain truth as a game
then: After all that clarity, the verse says the idolaters {trap}play about in doubt{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says the certain truth had come to them, but they doubted it and did not believe. Their doubt was not a search. It was a way of passing time.
now: You keep a few big questions open for years. You never sit down to look into them. You scroll instead. {trap}Doubt you never work on becomes a game you play.{/trap}
old: Staying undecided is the honest, safe position.
new: Doubt I never look into is just a way of not deciding.
try: Write down one question about faith you have carried for years. Find one honest answer this week.

title: Watch for the day the sky brings smoke.
subtitle: The sign that gives the surah its name
then: Ibn Mas'ud said Quraysh, stubborn against Islam, were struck with years of famine. {trap}They were so hungry that they saw only smoke between them and the sky.{/trap} Other reports, Ibn Kathir notes, make the Smoke one of the signs still awaited before the Hour.
now: You watch a news clip of wildfire haze over a city, people in masks. You talk about it and then move on. {idea}The verse says: watch.{/idea} Signs are for waking up, not just for discussing.
old: Big signs are for debating what they mean.
new: A sign is meant to change me, whatever its timing.
try: Next time hard news shakes you, pause and ask what it is asking of you.

title: It covers everyone. This is a painful punishment.
subtitle: When no one can stand outside it

row.title: it covers people
sub: so I check my own state

then: Ibn Kathir points out that the verse says {trap}covering mankind{/trap}, which he takes to mean something all will see, not only Makkah's hungry. The words this is a painful torment are said to them as a rebuke.
now: A storm alert flashes on every phone in the city at once. Nobody is "too important" for it. {idea}What touches everyone makes you look at yourself first{/idea}, not at who deserves it.
old: Warnings like this are about other people.
new: When it covers everyone, the only question is how I am standing.
try: Ask Allah tonight, in your own words, for safety for yourself and the people around you.

title: Remove it, Lord, and we will believe.
subtitle: Promises made only under pressure

row.title: before the crisis
sub: when it is still a choice

then: Ibn Kathir says when disbelievers witness Allah's punishment, {trap}they ask for it to be removed and promise to believe{/trap}. He links it to those who will wish to be sent back so they would not deny again.
now: The hospital corridor at 2 a.m. You promise: if they pull through, I will pray every prayer. Then they pull through. {idea}The verse asks what your faith looks like on an ordinary Tuesday.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about faith when I really need it.
new: Faith that only appears in a crisis is a bargain, not a bond.
try: Recall one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Keep a small piece of it today.

title: How can a reminder help them now?
subtitle: The clear Messenger had already come
then: The people asking for relief and promising faith {reward}had already had a clear Messenger ﷺ among them{/reward}, explaining things plainly. The verse asks how a reminder can help someone who {trap}turned from it when it came{/trap}.
now: You keep saying you will listen when someone explains it properly. Meanwhile the lecture link sits unopened in your messages. {idea}The reminder is already in your pocket.{/idea}
old: I would act if the message were clearer.
new: The message was clear. I was not listening.
try: Open one reminder someone sent you weeks ago and actually watch or read it.

title: They turned away and called him tutored and mad.
subtitle: Labels that make listening unnecessary
then: Quraysh did not answer the message. {trap}They turned away and attached labels to the Messenger ﷺ{/trap}: someone taught him, he is mad. Once a label sticks, nobody has to think about the words.
now: A colleague raises a fair point in a meeting. Someone mutters "she always complains" and the room moves on. {trap}A label is the fastest way to stop listening.{/trap}
old: I know what kind of person they are, so I can ignore them.
new: Labelling a speaker is often how I avoid a true message.
try: Next time you want to dismiss someone, repeat their point back to yourself fairly first.

title: The pain lifted a little, and they went back.
subtitle: Relief that ends the promise
then: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for rain for Mudar, who were dying. He prayed and the rain came. Ibn Mas'ud said {trap}when they were granted ease, they returned to their former state{/trap}. The verse had already said it: We will lift it a little, and you will go back.
now: The scan comes back clear. The debt is paid. In a month, the habits you swore off are back. {idea}Ease is the moment the promise is really tested.{/idea}
old: Once things get better, I can relax.
new: Relief is the real test of what I promised in the hard days.
try: Think of one thing that got easier recently and thank Allah with one concrete act.

title: The day of the great seizing will come.
subtitle: Respite does not mean it was forgotten
then: After the respite, Allah warned of {trap}a day of the great seizing{/trap}. Ibn Mas'ud said it was the day of Badr. Ibn Abbas said it is the Day of Resurrection, which Ibn Kathir calls the apparent meaning. Either way, the delay was time given, not a pardon.
now: You did something wrong years ago and nothing happened. You almost forgot. {idea}Quiet years are not a verdict. They are time to set it right{/idea} while you still can.
old: If nothing happened, it must not have mattered.
new: Delay is time given to me to come back, not a sign it was ignored.
try: Make one thing right that you have let slide because no one noticed.
